Coach Launch · Slide Themes

Six themes. Same twenty molds underneath — same structure, same beats, same plan table. What changes is the colour, the type, and the feel. Pick the one that suits your business, or pick the closest and let the builder overlay your own brand colours on top of it.

How this works. A theme is a set of tokens, not a separate deck. Every one of the twenty molds reads its colours, fonts and corner treatment from a single CL-THEME-TOKENS block — so switching theme rewrites one block in every slide and nothing else. Your words never move. That's why you can say "rebuild in Sovereign" and have the whole deck change look in minutes, with every headline still exactly as you approved it.

Theme, then brand. A theme is the starting point. If your Visual Style Guide has your own hero colour and fonts, the builder overlays them onto the theme you picked — you keep the theme's proportions, corners and character, and get your own palette. Pick on feel; the colour can follow you.

Crimson

crimsonDefault

The Coach Launch house look. Confident, modern, high contrast. Montserrat headlines over Lato body, generous corners, the signature crimson. Suits: anyone who wants the system's own look and doesn't want to think about it.

Ink

ink

Editorial restraint. A serif headline on warm paper, square corners, one deep oxblood accent used sparingly. Reads like a considered document rather than a pitch. Suits: consultants, advisors, authors, anyone selling judgement rather than energy.

Ember

ember

Warm and approachable. Terracotta on a cream canvas, soft rounded corners, a friendly geometric headline. Feels like a conversation, not a sales page. Suits: life, health and relationship coaches — anywhere trust matters more than swagger.

Sovereign

sovereign

Navy and gold. A high serif headline, near-square corners, gold used as a precious accent rather than a highlighter. The accent slides go navy, not gold, so the money slides read as expensive instead of loud. Suits: high-ticket finance, wealth, legacy and executive work.

Voltage

voltage

Dark all the way through. A slate deck with an electric cyan accent and a technical grotesque headline. The whole presentation runs dark, which reads sharp on a big screen and stops a bright room washing you out. Suits: technical, operations, agency and B2B audiences.

Meadow

meadow

Bright and optimistic. A clean green on white with a rounded modern headline and open spacing. High energy without shouting. Suits: fitness, wellness, nutrition, and any audience that skews younger or wants momentum rather than gravitas.
